ref: The relation between roots of the quadratic equation and coefficients SolvedEx.2
stem: The difference between the roots of the equation \(x^2 - 13x + k = 0\) is 7 find \(k\).
solution:
Comparing \(x^2 - 13x + k = 0\) with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\)

\(a = 1\), \(b = -13\), \(c = k\)

Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be the roots of the equation.

\(\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{b}{a} = -\dfrac{(-13)}{1} = 13\) ... (I)

But \(\alpha - \beta = 7\) ......... (given) (II)

\(2\alpha = 20\) ... (adding (I) and (II))

\(\therefore\) \(\alpha = 10\)

\(\therefore\) \(10 + \beta = 13\) ... (from (I))

\(\therefore\) \(\beta = 13 - 10\)

\(\therefore\) \(\beta = 3\)

But \(\alpha \times \beta = \dfrac{c}{a}\)

\(\therefore\) \(10 \times 3 = \dfrac{k}{1}\)

\(\therefore\) \(k = 30\)
